title: Signal yield and coupling limits
left_kicker: From the yield limit to ε²
main_equation_latex: \epsilon^2_{\rm up}=\frac{2\alpha N_f N_{\rm sig}^{\rm up}}{3\pi m_{A\prime} f_{\rm rad}\left(dN_{\rm bkg}/dm\right)}
citation_footer: BEST, Phys. Rev. D 80, 075018 (2009), Eq. (19), rearranged.
plot_caption: Observed 90% limits; visible branching correction included.
notes: BEST = Bjorken, Essig, Schuster and Toro. Their Eq. (19) is a differential signal-to-radiative-trident cross-section ratio integrated over full mass width δm, assuming Γ ≪ δm ≪ m. The displayed equation is its rearrangement into yield-limit notation. The density form follows after substituting N_rad = f_rad(dN_bkg/dm)δm and canceling δm; N_rad and δm need not appear on the slide.
N_rad = f_rad (dN_bkg/dm) δm, so δm cancels in the density form used by the analysis. N_sig^up = A90 is the full-template signal yield. Do not apply an additional extraction-window fraction.
The density uses ±1.64σ; the GP training exclusion and signal extraction use ±2.25σ. δm denotes the full normalization width, not σ or a half-width.

For the electron channel, interpret the paper's species factor as the phase-space-aware N_f = Γtot/Γee = 1/BR(A′→e⁺e⁻). It equals one below 2mμ and approximately 1.725 at 250 MeV in the minimal visible model. The preserved plot already has this correction; do not multiply the plot again.

α is the fine-structure constant. The historical reference slide uses the same yield-limit notation and boxed-left-equation/right-plot composition, without K_d. Its old confidence level and result claims are not transferred.
